stem.text: Let \( f(x) = x^{2} - 10 x + \frac{67}{4} \) and \( g(x) = 3 - 2 x \). Find the exact total area of the regions between the graphs of f and g from \( x = 1 \) to \( x = \frac{13}{2} \).

worked_solution.text: \( f(x) - g(x) = \left(x - \frac{11}{2}\right) \left(x - \frac{5}{2}\right) \), so the graphs cross at \( x = \frac{5}{2} \) and \( x = \frac{11}{2} \), both inside the interval. f is above g before the first crossing and after the second, and below g between them.
worked_solution.rule_named: intersections and order of the curves

worked_solution.text: The pieces are \( \int_{1}^{\frac{5}{2}} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{9}{2} \), \( \int_{\frac{5}{2}}^{\frac{11}{2}} \left(g(x) - f(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{9}{2} \) and \( \int_{\frac{11}{2}}^{\frac{13}{2}} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{11}{6} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: area of each piece, upper minus lower

worked_solution.text: The total area is the sum of the pieces, \( \frac{65}{6} \).

options.derivation: the curves split correctly but each piece integrated as lower minus upper
the crossing at x = 11/2 missed, so the second integral runs from 5/2 to 13/2 across it
f(x) - g(x) integrated once over the whole interval, across both crossings
